M1.title: listener taste profile
M1.question: For each listener, how many recordings did they start, finish, save and skip, and how much of the audio they started did they hear?
M1.need: CROSSFADE learns listener taste from what they actually play: how much of each recording they hear, whether they finish it, and whether they save or skip it (RA: Overview, "learning listener taste"; Play).
M1.requirement_text: an associative table and the two tables it relates, joined with INNER JOIN
M1.sql:
SELECT l.listener_id,
       l.display_name,
       COUNT(*) AS plays,
       SUM(CASE WHEN p.completed = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_plays,
       SUM(CASE WHEN p.reaction = 'saved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS saves,
       SUM(CASE WHEN p.reaction = 'skipped' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS skips,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(p.seconds_played) / SUM(t.duration), 1) AS pct_of_audio_heard
FROM crossfade.play AS p
INNER JOIN crossfade.listener AS l ON l.listener_id = p.listener_id
INNER JOIN crossfade.track AS t ON t.track_id = p.track_id
GROUP BY l.listener_id, l.display_name
ORDER BY pct_of_audio_heard DESC,
         l.listener_id

M2.title: royalty run: what each artist is owed
M2.question: In this royalty run, how much does each artist earn from the plays of their recordings, and how many of those plays qualified?
M2.need: CROSSFADE pays every artist a per-stream royalty from an exact ledger: each play keeps the royalty it earned when it was recorded, so a later rate change never rewrites what is owed (RA: Overview; Play: Royalty Amount; rule I7).
M2.requirement_text: two or more tables joined with LEFT OUTER JOIN
M2.sql:
SELECT a.artist_id,
       a.stage_name AS payee,
       COUNT(p.track_id) AS plays,
       SUM(CASE WHEN p.seconds_played >= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS qualifying_plays,
       IFNULL(SUM(p.royalty_amount), 0) AS usd_owed
FROM crossfade.artist AS a
LEFT OUTER JOIN crossfade.track AS t ON t.artist_id = a.artist_id
LEFT OUTER JOIN crossfade.play AS p ON p.track_id = t.track_id
GROUP BY a.artist_id, a.stage_name
ORDER BY usd_owed DESC,
         a.artist_id

M3.title: station reach
M3.question: How many listeners does each station reach, its creator included, and which stations have been shared beyond their creator?
M3.need: stations can be shared, and a shared station appears under its creator's display name (RA: Listener: Display Name; Station: Name; rule I6, "A play's Station ID may refer to a station created by another listener").
M3.requirement_text: a set operation (UNION, INTERSECT or EXCEPT)
M3.sql:
SELECT s.station_id,
       s.name AS station,
       l.display_name AS created_by,
       COUNT(*) AS listeners_reached,
       CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 1 THEN 'shared' ELSE 'creator only' END AS reach_status
FROM (SELECT station_id, listener_id
      FROM crossfade.station
      UNION
      SELECT station_id, listener_id
      FROM crossfade.play
      WHERE station_id IS NOT NULL) AS r
INNER JOIN crossfade.station AS s ON s.station_id = r.station_id
INNER JOIN crossfade.listener AS l ON l.listener_id = s.listener_id
GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name, l.display_name
ORDER BY listeners_reached DESC,
         s.station_id

M4.title: recordings the models disagree on
M4.question: Which recordings do the model versions place in different top genres, and how far apart are their distributions?
M4.need: CROSSFADE places every recording between genres; each model version returns a distribution with measures of how uncertain and how inconsistent it is, and model divergence records how far one version sits from the others that scored the same recording (RA: Overview; Track Score: Model Divergence).
M4.requirement_text: a subquery with a multi-row operation (IN, NOT IN, ANY, SOME, ALL or EXISTS)
M4.sql:
SELECT t.track_id,
       t.title,
       (SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM crossfade.track_score AS sc
        WHERE sc.track_id = t.track_id) AS models_scoring,
       (SELECT MAX(sd.model_divergence)
        FROM crossfade.track_score AS sd
        WHERE sd.track_id = t.track_id) AS highest_divergence
FROM crossfade.track AS t
WHERE t.track_id IN (SELECT s.track_id
                     FROM crossfade.track_score AS s
                     GROUP BY s.track_id
                     HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.genre_id) > 1)
ORDER BY highest_divergence DESC,
         t.track_id

M5.title: filling each station
M5.question: For each station, which recordings qualify under its model, window and blend, in what order, and how long would the station run?
M5.need: a station stores a genre blend and an ambiguity window, not a fixed list, and the service "returns recordings that genuinely occupy that region" (RA: Overview; Station). Which recordings belong on a station has to be worked out from the business plan's own rules, so the query applies each of them in turn: 1. only scored recordings can be streamed (RA: Track: Ingest Status); 2. a station is evaluated against its one nominated model version, "so that a station's contents do not change meaning when a different version scores the catalogue" (RA: Scoring Model 1:N Station); 3. the recording's posterior entropy must lie inside the station's window: the minimum excludes recordings "that sit squarely inside a single genre", the maximum those "the models cannot place with any confidence" (RA: Minimum and Maximum Ambiguity); 4. its top genre must be one of the station's blend genres (RA: Station Blend). The RA stores the top genre and the entropy on the scoring result "so that stations can filter without reading ten rows per score" (RA: Track Score), so the filter reads track_score, not the ten genre_probability rows. The RA does not rank qualifying recordings, so the query orders them by the station's own preference: the blend weight of their top genre, highest first (RA: Weight, "the share of the station's blend given to this genre"), then the higher posterior entropy, the recording further between genres, which is the service's selling point; track_id breaks ties.
M5.requirement_text: a derived table defined with WITH
M5.sql:
WITH eligible AS (
    SELECT st.station_id,
           st.name AS station,
           t.track_id,
           t.title,
           t.duration,
           g.name AS top_genre,
           b.weight AS genre_weight,
           s.posterior_entropy
    FROM crossfade.station AS st
    INNER JOIN crossfade.track_score AS s ON s.model_id = st.model_id
    INNER JOIN crossfade.track AS t ON t.track_id = s.track_id
    INNER JOIN crossfade.station_blend AS b ON b.station_id = st.station_id
                                           AND b.genre_id = s.genre_id
    INNER JOIN crossfade.genre AS g ON g.genre_id = s.genre_id
    WHERE t.ingest_status = 'scored'
      AND s.posterior_entropy BETWEEN st.minimum_ambiguity AND st.maximum_ambiguity
),
station_length AS (
    SELECT station_id,
           COUNT(*) AS recordings,
           ROUND(SUM(duration) / 60, 1) AS run_minutes
    FROM eligible
    GROUP BY station_id
)
SELECT e.station_id,
       e.station,
       e.track_id,
       e.title,
       e.top_genre,
       e.genre_weight,
       e.posterior_entropy,
       sl.recordings AS station_recordings,
       sl.run_minutes AS station_run_minutes
FROM eligible AS e
INNER JOIN station_length AS sl ON sl.station_id = e.station_id
ORDER BY e.station_id,
         e.genre_weight DESC,
         e.posterior_entropy DESC,
         e.track_id

M6.title: results to recompute
M6.question: Which released recordings have no scoring result from the model version now in service, and how far out of date is their newest result?
M6.need: every recording is scored by the model version in service at ingest, and newer versions are deployed over time (RA: Scoring Model: the date a version "was placed in service and began scoring incoming uploads"). Scored On is kept for exactly one purpose: "to establish which results predate a model redeployment and must be recomputed" (RA: Track Score: Scored On).
M6.requirement_text: an associative table and the two tables it relates, joined with INNER JOIN
M6.sql:
SELECT t.track_id,
       t.title,
       COUNT(*) AS results,
       GROUP_CONCAT(m.version_label ORDER BY m.deployed_on, m.model_id SEPARATOR ', ') AS scored_by,
       MAX(s.scored_on) AS last_scored_on,
       DATEDIFF((SELECT MAX(n.deployed_on) FROM crossfade.scoring_model AS n), MAX(s.scored_on)) AS days_out_of_date
FROM crossfade.track_score AS s
INNER JOIN crossfade.track AS t ON t.track_id = s.track_id
INNER JOIN crossfade.scoring_model AS m ON m.model_id = s.model_id
WHERE t.ingest_status = 'scored'
GROUP BY t.track_id, t.title
HAVING MAX(s.scored_on) < (SELECT MAX(n.deployed_on) FROM crossfade.scoring_model AS n)
ORDER BY days_out_of_date DESC,
         t.track_id

M7.title: where each recording sits between genres
M7.question: For each scoring result, which genre is the runner-up to the top genre, how close is it, and does the recording change character partway through?
M7.need: the catalogue "is indexed by where a recording sits between genres rather than by a single genre label" (RA: Overview). Genre Probability "holds the full distribution that stations match against, which the single top genre on Track Score cannot express" (RA: Genre Probability), so placing a recording between genres means reading past its top genre to the genre it sits closest to next.
M7.requirement_text: a derived table defined with WITH
M7.sql:
WITH second_place AS (
    SELECT gp.track_id,
           gp.model_id,
           MAX(gp.probability) AS probability
    FROM crossfade.genre_probability AS gp
    INNER JOIN crossfade.track_score AS s ON s.track_id = gp.track_id
                                         AND s.model_id = gp.model_id
    WHERE gp.genre_id <> s.genre_id
    GROUP BY gp.track_id, gp.model_id
),
runner_up AS (
    SELECT gp.track_id,
           gp.model_id,
           MIN(gp.genre_id) AS genre_id,
           sp.probability
    FROM crossfade.genre_probability AS gp
    INNER JOIN second_place AS sp ON sp.track_id = gp.track_id
                                 AND sp.model_id = gp.model_id
                                 AND sp.probability = gp.probability
    INNER JOIN crossfade.track_score AS s ON s.track_id = gp.track_id
                                         AND s.model_id = gp.model_id
    WHERE gp.genre_id <> s.genre_id
    GROUP BY gp.track_id, gp.model_id, sp.probability
)
SELECT t.track_id,
       t.title,
       s.model_id,
       g1.name AS top_genre,
       s.top_probability,
       g2.name AS runner_up_genre,
       r.probability AS runner_up_probability,
       s.top_probability - r.probability AS margin,
       s.segment_variance
FROM crossfade.track_score AS s
INNER JOIN crossfade.track AS t ON t.track_id = s.track_id
INNER JOIN runner_up AS r ON r.track_id = s.track_id
                         AND r.model_id = s.model_id
INNER JOIN crossfade.genre AS g1 ON g1.genre_id = s.genre_id
INNER JOIN crossfade.genre AS g2 ON g2.genre_id = r.genre_id
ORDER BY margin,
         t.track_id,
         s.model_id

cases.doc:
A listener who has played nothing has no taste profile yet.
Why: every sample listener has plays, so the INNER JOIN never has to drop anyone.
Expect: listener 20990 (no plays) is not in the result; the 8 sample listeners are.

An abandoned, skipped play lowers the share of audio heard and counts as a skip, not a completion.
Why: the sample's top listener (20937) heard all of their one recording; a second, half-heard play must pull the
share down by duration, not by play count.
Expect: 20937 has 2 plays, 1 completed, 1 skip, and hears 100 * (189 + 107) / (189 + 214) = 73.4 percent.

An artist whose recordings nobody has played yet is listed, owed zero.
Why: the sample's one artist with no plays (1049) has no uploads either, so the second LEFT OUTER JOIN (track to
play) never has to keep a track with no plays.
Expect: artist 9002 with track 9401 and no plays: 0 plays, 0 qualifying, 0 owed, listed after every earning artist.

A play under 30 seconds counts as a play but not as a qualifying play (RA rule I7).
Why: checks the 30-second boundary: one play at 29 seconds, one at exactly 30.
Expect: artist 1048 (track 4829) gains 2 plays and 1 qualifying play; what it is owed grows by the two recorded
royalties (0.00000 and 0.00350).

A listener playing a station someone else created makes it shared, and equal reach orders by station_id.
Why: in the sample only two stations are shared; a third at the same reach checks the tie-break.
Expect: 20937 plays station 7713 (created by 20933): 7713 reaches 2, 'shared', listed between 7710 and 7714.

A station nobody has played yet still reaches its creator.
Why: every sample station has been played through, so the creator half of the UNION is never the only source.
Expect: station 7799 (created by 20938, no plays) is listed with 1 listener, 'creator only', created_by 'hito'.

A second model version that names a different top genre puts the recording on the list; equal divergence
orders by track_id.
Why: 4824 is scored by one version only in the sample, so it can never qualify; a disagreeing score with the
same divergence as 4828 (0.0421) checks the tie-break too.
Expect: 4824 joins with 2 models scoring, listed just before 4828.

With three versions scoring a recording, the highest of their divergences is reported.
Why: every listed sample recording is scored by exactly two versions, whose divergences from each other are the
same number, so MAX and MIN agree and a wrong aggregate would go unnoticed.
Expect: model 4 also scores 4821 (metal, divergence 0.2000): 4821 shows 3 models scoring, highest 0.2000.

Another version that agrees on the top genre does not make a disagreement.
Why: the IN subquery must count distinct top genres, not scores.
Expect: model 1 scores 4824 as genre 2, like model 4 did: the result is unchanged (3 recordings).

A disagreement whose divergence is not recorded is still listed, after every measured one.
Why: model_divergence may be NULL; MAX of NULLs is NULL, and MySQL sorts NULL last in a DESC order.
Expect: new recording 9500, scored rock by model 1 and jazz by model 2, both without divergence: listed last,
highest_divergence NULL.

A recording whose entropy equals the window's minimum or maximum is on the station; one just outside is not.
Why: no sample score falls exactly on a window edge, so BETWEEN's inclusive edges are never tested.
Expect: station 7798 (model 3, window 0.40 to 0.60, blend country 1.00) with four model-3 country scores:
4818 (0.6000) and 4817 (0.4000) are on it, higher entropy first; 4819 (0.3999) and 4820 (0.6001) are not.

A rejected recording stays off every station even if a model scored it.
Why: every scored row in the sample belongs to a scored recording, so the ingest-status rule is never needed.
Expect: rejected track 4831, scored by model 2 as genre 0 at entropy 0.5000 (inside station 7717's window and
blend), is not on 7717, which still holds 1 recording.

A station holds only recordings whose top genre is in its blend, as placed by its own model version.
Why: a new station with a one-genre blend and the widest window isolates the blend and model rules.
Expect: station 7797 (model 4, window 0 to 1, blend genre 8 only) holds just 4825 (model 4 places it in genre 8;
model 1 also does, but model 1 is not this station's model): 1 recording, 4825's duration in minutes.

A recording scored by the version now in service no longer needs recomputing, whatever its older results.
Why: only the newest result matters; the sample's oldest stale recording (4819) is rescored here.
Expect: beardown_3sec (model 5) scores 4819 on 2026-07-01: 4819 leaves the list, which keeps the other 8.

A result scored at midnight on the deployment day is up to date; one second earlier is not.
Why: deployed_on is a date, scored_on a moment; the comparison puts the deployment at 00:00:00 of that day.
Expect: 4819 rescored by model 5 at 2026-06-23 00:00:00 leaves the list; 4821 rescored at 2026-06-22 23:59:59
stays, 1 day out of date, now scored by 3 versions.

Deploying a new version makes every released, scored recording due for recomputing, and equal ages order
by track_id.
Why: in the sample the newest version already scored 4 recordings; a version deployed after every result
leaves none up to date.
Expect: version 6 deployed 2026-08-01: all 13 scored recordings are listed, the days counted from 2026-08-01.

A rejected recording is not queued for recomputing, however old its result.
Why: none of the sample's scored results belongs to a rejected recording.
Expect: rejected 4831 scored by model 1 in January: not listed; the 9 sample rows are unchanged.

When two genres share the runner-up probability, the lower genre_id is the runner-up, and the result
appears once.
Why: no sample distribution has a tie for second place; without the rule the result would appear twice.
Expect: model 1 scores 4824 as country (2, 0.4000) with disco (3) and jazz (5) both at 0.2000: one row,
runner-up disco, margin 0.2000.

When two genres share the top probability, the other one is the runner-up and the margin is 0: the
recording sits exactly between them, and is listed first.
Why: the sample has no tied top genre; margin 0 is the strongest "between genres" case.
Expect: model 2 scores 4824 with pop (7) and rock (9) both at 0.4000 and pop as its top genre: runner-up rock,
margin 0.0000, first row.

A scoring result with no probability rows has no runner-up, so it is left out rather than shown half empty.
Why: rule I2 says every result has its ten probabilities, but the database alone does not stop a result being
written first; the INNER JOIN to the derived table drops it.
Expect: model 1 scores 4824 with no genre_probability rows: 4824 is listed only for model 4, as before.
